newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-ROWELL GAMBLES AS WALLABIES SUMMON MANU.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ROWELL GAMBLES AS WALLABIES SUMMON MANU.

text.p: England coach Jack Rowell has acknowledged the risk involved in relying on his tired but jubilant British Lions contingent for Saturday's one-off rugby union test against Australia.
Seven English players who featured in last Saturday's losing third test in the Lions' 2-1 series win over South Africa will face the Wallabies at the Sydney Football Stadium.

They include fly-half Mike Catt, scrum-half Matt Dawson, number eight Lawrence Dallaglio, full-back Tim Stimpson and former rugby league winger John Bentley who will play his first union test for England in nine years.
Rowell said there was no way of knowing whether the jet-lagged players would succumb to fatigue or be inspired by their success in beating the Springboks.
"The threat is that they will be physically and mentally jaded, whereas we need an overspill of confidence from the Lions tour" Rowell said.
"Whichever one of those proves to be the case will effectively decide how the game goes from an England point of view. But we won't know until Saturday," Rowell said.

Meanwhile, Australia coach Greg Smith finalised his team selection by naming flanker Daniel Manu to replace David Wilson, the seventh change from the side which lost 30-13 to New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday.
Smith has focused most of his attention on the forwards, drafting uncapped prop Cameron Blades, hooker Michael Foley and lock Garrick Morgan into the side to add scrummaging power.
Rowell was unhappy about the lack of time to prepare his side to tackle a Wallaby outfit determined to make amends for their heavy defeat by the All Blacks.
"The timing is not ideal. Obviously, this game coming on the end of a Lions tour is quite a challenge. The players have been away for eight weeks," Rowell said.
"It is the shortest amount of time we've had together before a match since the game turned professional two years ago," Rowell said.
"Even before then we would have had more time to get the effects of the travel out of the system. But these decisions have nothing to do with me or the players."

Centre Nick Greenstock, a member of England's second-string side which drew with Argentina in an away test series last month, replaces British Lions hero Jeremy Guscott, who broke his arm in the Lions' third test and returned home.
England will also be without prop Jason Leonard, lock and Lions captain Martin Johnson and winger Adedavo Adebayo because of injury, Rowell said.
England will stage a return test against Australia at Twickenham in November.

England - 15-Tim Stimpson, 14-John Bentley, 13-Phil de Glanville (captain), 12-Nick Greenstock, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Matthew Dawson; 8-Tim Rodber, 7-Richard Hill, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Nigel Redman, 3-Darren Garforth, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke, 14-Joe Roff, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Ben Tune; 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan, 8-Troy Coker, 7-Brett Robinson, 6-Daniel Manu, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Garrick Morgan, 3-Cameron Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Ewen McKenzie.
